items.sentence: If it rains tomorrow, the basketball game ___ cancelled.
items.why: A real future possibility uses 'if' + present, then 'will' in the result.

items.sentence: If I ___ rich, I would buy Nanay a house in the province.
items.why: An imagined situation uses 'were' after 'if', even with 'I' or 'she'.

items.sentence: If Lyka had studied for the quiz, she ___ passed.
items.why: A past that did not happen uses 'had' after 'if' and 'would have' in the result.

items.sentence: If you heat water to 100 degrees, it ___.
items.why: A fact that is always true uses the present tense in both parts.

items.sentence: Marco ___ join the basketball team if he were taller.
items.why: When the 'if' part uses 'were', the result uses 'would'.

items.sentence: If Kuya Ron ___ the bus, he will be late for work.
items.why: In a first conditional, the 'if' part stays in the present, and 'he' needs 'misses'.

items.sentence: If we had left earlier, we ___ caught the last jeepney.
items.why: 'If we had left' is about the past, so the result needs 'would have'.

items.sentence: If the signal is strong, the video ___ without buffering.
items.why: A general truth uses the present tense, and 'the video' needs 'loads'.

items.sentence: I would send more load to Bea if I ___ extra money.
items.why: When the result uses 'would', the 'if' part uses the past form 'had'.

items.sentence: If the typhoon ___ hit, classes would not have been cancelled.
items.why: 'Would not have been' points to the past, so the 'if' part needs 'had not'.

items.sentence: The classroom ___ cleaned by the Grade 8 students every Friday.
items.why: A regular passive action uses 'is' plus the past participle for a singular subject.

items.sentence: The new covered court ___ built last year by the barangay.
items.why: 'Last year' means the past, so the passive uses 'was' plus 'built'.

items.sentence: All the merienda ___ already been eaten by Jom's cousins.
items.why: 'Merienda' is singular, so the present perfect passive uses 'has been'.

items.sentence: The tricycle fare ___ by the drivers' association last month.
items.why: The fare did not do the action, so use the passive 'was raised'.

items.sentence: The exam papers ___ checked by Ma'am Reyes tonight.
items.why: A future passive uses 'will be' plus the past participle.

items.sentence: This TikTok dance ___ by millions of people every day.
items.why: The dance receives the action, so use 'is' plus the past participle 'watched'.

items.sentence: Lyka ___ chosen as the class representative yesterday.
items.why: 'Yesterday' means the past, and 'Lyka' is singular, so use 'was chosen'.

items.sentence: Our jeepney ___ by Kuya Ron, not by Tatay.
items.why: The jeepney does not drive itself, so the passive 'is driven' fits.

items.sentence: Tita Nena ___ the pancit for the fiesta herself.
items.why: Tita Nena did the action herself, so the active verb 'cooked' is correct.

items.sentence: The package from Nanay in Dubai ___ delivered yet.
items.why: 'Yet' goes with the present perfect, so use 'has not been' plus 'delivered'.

items.sentence: The teacher ___ coaches our basketball team is from Cebu.
items.why: Use 'who' for a person doing the action in the clause.

items.sentence: The sari-sari store ___ sells cheap load is closed today.
items.why: Use 'that' or 'which' for a thing, never 'who'.

items.sentence: Jom is the student ___ phone was stolen on the jeepney.
items.why: Use 'whose' to show that something belongs to someone.

items.sentence: The barangay hall is the place ___ we practice our dance.
items.why: Use 'where' when the clause tells about a place.

items.sentence: I still remember the day ___ the typhoon hit our town.
items.why: Use 'when' when the clause tells about a time.

items.sentence: The player ___ the coach praised is Marco's cousin.
items.why: Use 'whom' for a person who receives the action in the clause.

items.sentence: Bea bought a phone ___ has a very good camera.
items.why: Use 'which' for a thing like a phone, not 'who'.

items.sentence: Tita Nena, ___ works in Dubai, sends money every month.
items.why: Use 'who' for a person, even inside commas.

items.sentence: The online game ___ my brother plays is free to download.
items.why: A game is a thing, so use 'that' or 'which'.

items.sentence: The tricycle driver ___ we met at the fiesta is Lyka's uncle.
items.why: The driver is a person who received the action 'met', so use 'whom'.

items.sentence: Bea said she ___ tired after the long jeepney ride.
items.why: After 'said', the verb moves one step back, so 'is' becomes 'was'.

items.sentence: Marco ___ me that the game was cancelled.
items.why: Use 'told' when you name the person, like 'told me'.

items.sentence: Jom ___ that he could not buy load that week.
items.why: Use 'said' when no listener is named right after the verb.

items.sentence: Lyka asked ___ the quiz would be moved to Friday.
items.why: A reported yes-or-no question uses 'if' or 'whether'.

items.sentence: The coach told the players ___ early for practice.
items.why: A reported command uses 'told' plus a person plus 'to' and the verb.

items.sentence: Kuya Ron said he ___ send money after his first salary abroad.
items.why: In reported speech, 'will' moves back to 'would'.

items.sentence: Tita Nena asked me ___ I had eaten my merienda.
items.why: A reported yes-or-no question uses 'whether' or 'if', not 'that'.

items.sentence: Ma'am Reyes told us ___ our phones during the exam.
items.why: A reported negative command uses 'not to' plus the verb.

items.sentence: The driver said the tricycle fare ___ gone up again.
items.why: After 'said', 'has gone' moves back to 'had gone'.

items.sentence: Nanay ___ she would call from Dubai on Sunday.
items.why: Use 'said' before a reported sentence; 'told' always needs a person after it.
